''3. Becau{{ls}}e of Herodias.''] It is to ordinary in Princes to put them to death that freely tel them {{ls}}uch faultes: women, whom they fan{{ls}}ie, {{ls}}pecially inciting them to {{ls}}uch mi{{ls}}cheefe.

''12. Buried it.''] An example of duty toward the dead bodies of the faithful. Wherein {{ls}}ee the difference of Catholike Chri{{ls}}tian men and of al infidels, be they Pagans, Apo{{ls}}tataes, or Heretikes. For whereas the Chri{{ls}}tians had layd the body of this ble{{ls}}sed Prophete and Martyr {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Hiero. in Epitaph. Paulæ. c. 6''.}}* in Samaria with the Relikes of Elias and Abdias, by vertue wherof wōderful miracles were wrought in that place: in Iulian the Apo{{ls}}tataes time, when men might doe al mi{{ls}}cheefe freely again{{ls}}t Chri{{ls}}tian religion, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Sacrilege again{{ls}}t holy Relikes.}}the Pagans opened the tombe of S. Iohn Bapti{{ls}}t, burnt his bones, {{ls}}cattered the a{{ls}}hes about the fields: but certaine religious Monkes coming thither a pilgrimage at the {{ls}}ame time, aduentured their life and {{ls}}aued as much of the holy Relikes as they could, and brought them to their Abbot Philip a man of God: who e{{ls}}teeming them to great a trea{{ls}}ure for him and his, to keepe for their priuate deuotion, {{ls}}ent them to Athana{{ls}}ius the B. of Alexandria, and he with al reuerence layd them in {{ls}}uch a place (as it were by the Spirit of Prophecie) where afterward by occa{{ls}}ion of them was built a goodly chappel. ''Theod. li. 3 c. 6. Ruff. li. 2 c. 28''. 27. Marke here that the Heretikes of our time doe as tho{{ls}}e Pagans, to the bodies and Relikes of al ble{{ls}}sed Saints that they can de{{ls}}troy: and Catholikes contrariwi{{ls}}e haue the religious deuotion of tho{{ls}}e old Chri{{ls}}tians, as appeareth by the honour done now to his head at Amiens in France.

''13. Retired.''] Chri{{ls}}t much e{{ls}}teemed Iohn, and withdrewe him {{ls}}elf a{{ls}}ide, to giue example of moderate mourning for the departed, and to {{ls}}hew the horrour of that execrable murder. as in the Primitiue Churche many good men {{ls}}eing the mi{{ls}}erable {{ls}}tate of the world in the time of per{{ls}}ecution, and the {{ls}}innes that abounded withal: tooke an occa{{ls}}ion to for{{ls}}ake tho{{ls}}e tumults, and to giue them {{ls}}elues to contemplation: and for that purpo{{ls}}e retired into the de{{ls}}erts of Ægypt and els where, to doe penance for their owne {{ls}}innes and the {{ls}}innes of the world. Wherevpon partly ro{{ls}}e that infinite number of Monkes and Eremites, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Eremites.}}of whom the fathers and Eccle{{ls}}ia{{ls}}tical hi{{ls}}tories make mention. ''Hiero. to. 2 in vit. Pauli Eremitæ. Sozo. li. 1 c. 12. 13''.

''19. ''26. Walking.''] When not only Chri{{ls}}t, but by his power Peter al{{ls}}o walketh vpon the vvaters, it is euident that he can di{{ls}}po{{ls}}e of his owne body aboue nature and contrary to the natural conditions thereof, as to goe through a doore. ''Io. 20''. to be in the compa{{ls}}se of a litle bread. ''Epiphan. in Anchorato''.
